thread.title: UPDATE: Trade war's 'nuclear option' could be bad for Apple, Amazon: strategist

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Trade war's 'nuclear option' could be bad for Apple, Amazon: strategist
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
Stock market bulls have met trade-war headlines largely head on this year--pausing at times to snort and paw the ground before charging right through.
But as investors weigh up the White House's latest battle with China on trade, some are warning that this time, things could be different. Among them is our call of the day from Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading, who warns of dire consequences if China takes the "nuclear option" of restricting sales of materials, equipment and other key parts of U.S. manufacturers' supply chain.
"The disruption it would cause for the global economy and financial markets would be astounding. It would shift from a trade war to economic warfare by means of a scorched earth approach," O'Rourke told clients in a note.
Apple (AAPL) would be one of the big losers under those circumstances, he said.
Opinion: Apple Watch is safe, but China tariffs could still hit other consumer tech products (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-watch-is-safe-but-china-tariffs-could-still-hit-other-consumer-tech-products-2018-09-17)
"The number one product the U.S. imports from China is cellphones, a large portion of which are iPhones. Once the tariffs start effecting the prices of Apple's products and Main Street America, as well as corporate profits, the effects of the tariffs will feel much more tangible," says O'Rourke.
Apple's stock initially rallied Monday, spurred by news the iWatch and wireless earbuds were excluded from U.S. tariffs on $200 billion in Chinese goods. But the shares turned down once fears about China's retaliation took over and Apple ended the session down 2.7%.
Read:Latest U.S. tariffs won't affect Apple, but China's retaliation might (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/latest-us-tariffs-wont-affect-apple-but-chinas-retaliation-might-2018-09-17)
Lots of retailers, such as Amazon (AMZN) and Walmart (WMT), also have goods that will be in the tariff firing line, he said.
As for those who argue that China would be crazy to go "nuclear" and blow up its relationships with U.S. companies, O'Rourke says the country can simply argue that "it didn't start this war."
Read:Analysts say Apple's iPhone preorders stable or even down from last year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-stock-slips-as-analysts-say-iphone-preorders-appear-stable-or-down-from-last-year-2018-09-17) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-stock-slips-as-analysts-say-iphone-preorders-appear-stable-or-down-from-last-year-2018-09-17)
The market
The S&P , Dow and Nasdaq are all modestly higher.
Gold and crude are softer, while the dollar (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-finds-footing-as-us-china-trade-fight-intensifies-2018-09-18) is holding steady.
Europe is mostly firmer and Asia stocks had an upbeat day (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mostly-shrug-off-latest-us-tariffs-targeting-china-2018-09-17) with the Shanghai Composite rebounding from a nearly four-year low.
Check out the Market Snapshot column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-futures-edge-up-but-trade-uncertainty-remains-in-focus-2018-09-18) for more
The buzz
China responded, sort of, to the $200 billion in tariffs on its imports announced late Monday by the Trump administration (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-to-impose-another-200-billion-in-tariffs-on-chinese-goods-2018-09-17). The Commerce Ministry said on its website that it "has no choice but to undertake synchronous retaliation." Meanwhile, Alibaba's (BABA) chairman Jack Ma warned that the spat between the two countries could last two decades (https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-alibaba/alibabas-jack-ma-says-u-s-china-trade-war-could-last-for-20-years-idUSKCN1LY16Z?feedType=RSS&feedName=topNews&utm_source=feedburner&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=Feed%3A+reuters%2FtopNews+%28News+%2F+US+%2F+Top+News%29).
Japanese billionaire and entrepreneur Yusaku Maezawa will be SpaceX's first passenger to the moon (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/spacex-to-take-japanese-billionaire-yusaku-maezawa-to-the-moon-2018-09-17) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/spacex-to-take-japanese-billionaire-yusaku-maezawa-to-the-moon-2018-09-17) says CEO Elon Musk. And he wants artists to come along for the ride. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/spacex-to-take-japanese-billionaire-yusaku-maezawa-to-the-moon-2018-09-17)
(https://twitter.com/yousuck2020/status/1041868256464654336)
Oracle (ORCL) is under pressure after more disappointing cloud numbers cause a miss on revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oracle-earnings-show-another-cloud-miss-stock-falls-2018-09-17). (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oracle-earnings-show-another-cloud-miss-stock-falls-2018-09-17) FedEx (FDX) may also get dinged by a miss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fedex-misses-adjusted-eps-expectations-but-revenue-tops-views-2018-09-17).
Visa (V) and Mastercard (MA) have settled a class-action suit with U.S. retailers for a proposed $6.2 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/visa-mastercard-settle-us-retailers-class-action-suit-2018-09-18).
Cannibas cultivator Tilray has won approval from the DEA (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tilray-to-import-cannabis-to-us-for-clinical-trial-2018-09-18) to import a pot product from Canada to test how effective it is in treating a neurological disorder that affects millions of Americans.
Alphabet's Google (GOOGL) is teaming up with a big auto alliance to provide infotainment systems for their cars and Amazon (AMZN) reportedly plans to launch an Alexa-powered microwave (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amazon-to-launch-alexa-powered-microwave-other-gadgets-report-2018-09-17) and other gadgets.
"Black Mirror" and other hits brought home the Emmys (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/2018-emmy-awards-netflix-and-amazon-clean-up-plus-complete-list-of-winners-2018-09-17) on Monday night for Netflix (NFLX), which tied with AT&T's (T) HBO for most nominations this year. Amazon (AMZN) also didn't come out too shabby with wins for "The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel."
A home builders index will be out this morning after the market opens.
The chart
How bullish are investors about U.S. stocks? Our chart of the day from Bank of America Merrill Lynch's latest fund manager survey (from Sept. 7 to 13) finds that portfolio managers are the most overweight they've been on the asset class since January 2015.
The Quote:
"The idea that I am kneeling in water to make it look deep is, frankly, idiotic."--That was CNN's Anderson Cooper firing back at a photo tweeted by Donald Trump Jr (https://edition.cnn.com/videos/politics/2018/09/18/donald-trump-jr-anderson-cooper-debunks-florence-twitter-photo-kth-sot-ac.cnn)., which suggested the anchor was faking Hurricane Florence floodwaters to make his dad POTUS look bad. He explained the picture actually was of extensive flooding from Hurricane Ike in 2008. And no, he says he wasn't kneeling.
(https://twitter.com/DonaldJTrumpJr/status/1041310008623943680)
Random reads
This proposal (https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2018/09/emmys-proposal-2018-glenn-weiss-director-jan-svendsen) pretty much stole the show at the Emmys
(https://twitter.com/NYMag/status/1041865777173823488)
The U.S. will cap refugees at a record low of 30,000 next year (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/09/slashes-number-refugees-admit-30000-180917225659912.html)
Russia points a finger at Israel (https://www.wsj.com/articles/russia-blames-israel-for-military-plane-shot-down-over-syria-1537260656?mod=hp_lead_pos4) over a military plane shot down late Monday
